## Purpose

Your team will present its [Team Project](../team-project.qmd) to the class. This assignment is the slide deck. The in-class presentation itself is graded separately (100 points) on **November 6 or November 13**; its rubric is below.

Being a strong presenter is a skill you will use throughout your academic and professional career, whether you are defending a thesis, pitching an idea, or presenting research at a conference.

## The Presentation

- **Length: 15 minutes per team**, about 12 minutes of presentation and 3 minutes of questions. We will hold you to time, so rehearse with a timer.
- **Every team member presents**, for roughly equal time. Plan your hand-offs.
- **Questions** come from the class, the Team Leader, and the instructor, and may be directed to any team member.
- Aim for about **10&ndash;15 content slides**, plus a title slide, a references slide, and the Verification Form slide.

A typical structure:

| Track A: Inside a Physics Lab | Track B: Measure Tech |
|---|---|
| The research question and why it matters | The question and why it is interesting |
| How the group answers it: apparatus, methods, or models | Method 1 and Method 2: how you did them |
| What you saw and learned on your visit | Your results, with uncertainties |
| The people: their paths into physics | Do your methods agree? Why or why not? |
| How a first-year can get involved | What went wrong, and what you would change |

## What to Submit

- The team's final slide deck, submitted as a PDF named `Team-Name-Slides.pdf`.
- **All teams submit by November 6**, including teams presenting on November 13.
- One team member uploads the PDF to Canvas. Every member is responsible for confirming that it was submitted.

## Expectations

**Analyze.** Understand the assignment and your audience: your classmates. Define terms they may not know.

**Show your experience.** Your deck must include the evidence described in the [Team Project](../team-project.qmd#evidence-of-your-work): your own dated photos or video of your team doing the work, and a photo or scan of the signed Verification Form as the last slide.

**Research.** Use reliable sources and cite them on a references slide. Label any image that is not your own with its source.

**Plan.** Give the presentation a clear beginning, middle, and end. Every slide should support the main point.

**Design.** Keep text short; slides support what you say rather than repeat it. Use figures and images where they explain something better than words. For Track B, show your data in a plot with labeled axes and units.

**Practice together.** Rehearse the full presentation as a team, out loud, at least once. This is how you catch gaps, redundancies, and rough hand-offs between speakers.

**Present.** Every team member presents. Speak to the audience, make eye contact, and **never read your slides**.

## Rubric

### Slides (100 points)

| Criterion | Points |
|---|---|
| **Content.** The question, approach, and findings are clear and accurate, and explained at the level of a first-year physics student. | 30 |
| **Evidence of first-hand work.** Your own dated photos or video of the team doing the work, and the signed Verification Form. | 30 |
| **Organization.** Clear beginning, middle, and end; each slide supports the main point. | 15 |
| **Design.** Readable text, little of it; figures and plots that are labeled and explain something. | 15 |
| **Sources.** Background and outside images are cited on a references slide. | 10 |
| **Total** | **100** |

### Presentation (100 points)

| Criterion | Points |
|---|---|
| **Delivery.** Speakers talk to the audience, make eye contact, and do not read the slides. | 30 |
| **Teamwork.** Every member presents a fair share; hand-offs are smooth. | 20 |
| **Questions.** Any team member can answer questions about any part of the project. | 20 |
| **Timing.** The presentation fits in the 15-minute slot. | 15 |
| **Process.** The team completed its check-in with the Team Leader by October 23. | 15 |
| **Total** | **100** |

## Submission Checklist

- The deck has a title slide with the team name, the track, and all members' names.
- The deck includes our own dated photos or video of the team doing the work.
- The last slide is a photo or scan of the signed Verification Form.
- Sources are cited on a references slide.
- The team has rehearsed the full presentation together, with a timer.
- The deck is submitted as a single PDF by November 6.
